newsitem.title: USA: Coleman names chairman, sees fourth quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: Coleman names chairman, sees fourth quarter loss.

text.p: Coleman Co. Inc., the maker of stoves and other camping gear, Tuesday named former Chairman Jerry Levin as acting chief executive officer and said it expected losses for the fourth quarter and year.
Coleman said Levin would succeed Michael Hammes, who is leaving the Golden, Colo.-based company. Levin, a former chairman of Coleman, has been a director of the company since 1989.
Levin is also executive vice president of MacAndrews & Forbes Holdings Inc., which owns about 83 percent of Coleman's outstanding common stock, and chairman of Revlon Inc.
Coleman said it was seeking a permanent chief executive officer and Levin will stay on as chairman after the search is over.

Coleman also said it expected to report a net loss of about $37 million for the quarter and a loss of about $45 million for all of 1996. Coleman reported net income of $39 million or 74 cents a share for 1995.

Coleman said the expected loss was due mainly to one-time factors, including the costs of integrating the Camping Gaz operations into the company. It bought a 60 percent stake in Camping Gaz from France's Butagaz in February 1996.
Coleman also had to pay $3.7 million to Black & Decker Corp. after it settled a patent infringement lawsuit. Coleman said it took other unspecified charges for discontinued products.

It said it expected operating income of about $70 million before restructuring and other charges. The restructuring and other charges previously announced in the third quarter and additional charges in connection with the patent settlement total about $55 million after taxes.
Its stock fell 50 cents to $11.75 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.
